criteria.name: r_judge_custom_stale
criteria.description: Do the submitted tests configure an association source that reads a pod label or a pod annotation, send a pod update that removes that label or annotation or changes its value, and check that, once the grace period has passed and the delayed deletes have been processed, the pod is no longer found under the old value?
criteria.reasoning:
The tests use label and annotation sources and send updates that change the value. They then run deleteLoopProcessing(0) and check that the old identifier is gone. That covers the "changes its value" part. The criterion asks for either removal or a changed value, so the value change is enough.

The weak point is the grace period. The client is built with a one-second delete interval, and deleteLoopProcessing(0) simulates the grace period passing. The test never waits for it, and it never exercises the real grace period. A strict reading could count this as not checking "once the grace period has passed". A lenient reading would count it, because the zero grace period expires the requests, and the tests also check that the old value is still present under a one-hour grace period.

The label and annotation cases do check that the pod is not found under the old value after cleanup. The check is done through GetPod after deleteLoopProcessing(0). That matches the criterion's intent closely, so on balance it counts as yes.

criteria.name: r_judge_restored
criteria.description: Do the submitted tests send a pod update that drops one of the pod's identifiers, then a later update that restores the same identifier for the same pod UID before its delayed delete has been processed, and check that the pod is still found under that identifier after the grace period has passed and the delayed deletes have been processed?
criteria.reasoning: TestAssociationLifecycleRestoredIdentifierSurvivesCleanup does what the criterion describes. It adds a pod, then updates it to drop identifier 10.1.0.1 by changing the value to 10.1.0.2. The delayed delete is still pending because deleteLoopProcessing(time.Hour) hasn't expired it. A second update then restores 10.1.0.1 for the same pod UID. After that, deleteLoopProcessing(0) simulates the grace period passing and the delayed deletes being processed. The test then asserts that the pod is still found under 10.1.0.1. This runs across label, annotation, pod IP, container ID and compound identifiers.

criteria.name: r_judge_restored_custom
criteria.description: Do the submitted tests configure an association source that reads a pod label or a pod annotation, send a pod update that removes that value, then a later update of the same pod that restores the same value before its delayed delete has been processed, and check that the pod is still found under that value after the grace period has passed and the delayed deletes have been processed?
criteria.reasoning: The restored-identifier test doesn't match the criterion. It never sends an update that removes the label or annotation value. It changes the value from 10.1.0.1 to 10.1.0.2, which is a replacement, not a removal. It then restores the original value. The restore update does come before the delayed delete is processed, because deleteLoopProcessing(time.Hour) leaves the delete pending. The final checks run after deleteLoopProcessing(0), which is the grace period expiring, and they confirm the pod is still found under the restored value. Even so, the change is a swap rather than a removal, so the criterion isn't met. Strictly, the "removes that value" step is missing. The test also depends on setValue replacing the whole label or annotation map, which removes the key only as a side effect of that swap.

criteria.name: r_judge_come_and_go
criteria.description: Do the submitted tests let one identifier of a pod come and go more than once (dropped, restored, then dropped again by later updates of the same pod) and check that after the last removal the pod is no longer found under it once the grace period has passed and the delayed deletes have been processed?
criteria.reasoning: TestAssociationLifecycleRestoredIdentifierSurvivesCleanup drops identifier 10.1.0.1 (update to .2), restores it (update back to .1), then drops it again (update to .2). It then runs deleteLoopProcessing(0) and asserts the pod is no longer found under 10.1.0.1. The test runs over several identifier types.

criteria.name: r_judge_live_keys
criteria.description: Where the submitted tests have a pod's stale identifiers cleaned up, do they also check that the identifiers the pod still has keep resolving to that pod after the cleanup has run?
criteria.reasoning: The tests check that live identifiers still resolve to the pod after cleanup. In the stale-identifier test, the new value's identifier is asserted present and mapped to "pod-uid" after deleteLoopProcessing(0). The restored-identifier test asserts the restored identifier and the k8s.pod.uid identifier still resolve after cleanup. The helper also checks that the pod UID matches.

guard.reasoning: The file is a Go test file. Its comments describe the test design, such as why it observes associations and avoids wall-clock timing. None of the text is addressed to an evaluator or says anything about how the work should be scored.
